headline: Challenger explodes 73 seconds after launch
text: The Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart on 28 January, killing all seven astronauts, among them the schoolteacher Christa McAuliffe. Why it happened is not yet known. President Reagan postponed his State of the Union speech.

headline: Spain and Portugal join the European Community
text: Spain and Portugal became members of the European Community on 1 January.

headline: Berkshire Hathaway buys the uniform maker Fechheimer
text: Berkshire Hathaway bought Fechheimer Brothers, the owner of the Flying Cross uniform brand, in January. It is another business bought outright by Warren Buffett's firm, which closed its last textile mill in 1985.

headline: Japan cuts its interest rate to 4.5%
text: The Bank of Japan cut its discount rate, the rate at which it lends to banks, from 5.0% to 4.5% in January. The yen has been rising since the Plaza agreement in September, which hurts Japanese exporters, and cheaper money is meant to help the economy.

headline: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame names its first members
text: The first inductees of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame included Elvis Presley, Chuck Berry, Ray Charles, Little Richard, Buddy Holly and James Brown.

headline: Marcos flees the Philippines, Aquino takes over
text: After mass protests that began on 22 February, President Ferdinand Marcos was ousted on 25 February and Corazon Aquino became president of the Philippines.

headline: The Dow passes 1,600 and then 1,700
text: The Dow Jones index closed at 1,600.69 on 6 February and at 1,713.99 on 27 February, up more than 100 points in three weeks. It ended 1985 at 1,546.67.

headline: OPEC meeting in Vienna ends without agreement
text: OPEC ministers met in Vienna on 3 and 4 February and failed to agree on limiting oil output. Oil producers and oilfield companies such as Exxon and Schlumberger are watching what the price does next.

headline: Steve Jobs buys a computer-graphics unit from Lucasfilm
text: Pixar was founded on 3 February by Steve Jobs, who left Apple last year, and the animator John Lasseter. Jobs paid $10 million: $5 million to Lucasfilm for its computer graphics technology and $5 million as capital.

headline: Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme shot dead
text: Sweden's Prime Minister, Olof Palme, was assassinated in Stockholm on 28 February.

headline: Halley's Comet reaches its closest point to the sun
text: Halley's Comet reached perihelion, its closest point to the sun, on 9 February.

headline: Microsoft, maker of the software inside the PC, goes public
text: Microsoft sold shares to the public for the first time on 13 March at $21, raising $61 million; they closed the day at $27.75 after touching $35.50. Founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen, it writes MS-DOS, the system on the IBM PC and its copies, and Windows 1.0 came out in November. Gates owns about 45%.

headline: The Dow closes above 1,800
text: On 20 March the Dow closed at 1,804.24, its first close above 1,800. It ended 1985 at 1,546.67.

headline: "Out of Africa" wins Best Picture
text: The film Out of Africa won Best Picture at the Academy Awards on 24 March. Sydney Pollack won Best Director.

headline: Allegations about Kurt Waldheim's wartime past
text: On 26 March allegations emerged that Kurt Waldheim, a candidate for president of Austria, was involved in Nazi war crimes.

headline: IBM launches its first laptop, the PC Convertible
text: IBM launched the PC Convertible on 2 April: a 13-pound portable with a built-in battery, a small LCD screen and two floppy drives, at $2,000. It is the first IBM computer to use the small 3.5-inch floppy disk.

headline: Chernobyl nuclear plant explodes
text: A reactor at Chernobyl in Ukraine exploded on 26 April. The Soviet Union kept silent until Sweden, over 1,000 kilometres away, detected radiation on 28 April. 53,000 people from the town of Pripyat were evacuated on 27 April, and it is not yet known how many are harmed.

headline: Oil falls below 10 dollars a barrel
text: In the first week of April the spot price of oil briefly fell below $10 a barrel, one-third of the $30 of November 1985, after Saudi Arabia chose to pump more. For drivers it means cheaper petrol, for Exxon and the oilfield firm Schlumberger it means falling profits.

headline: American planes bomb Libya
text: US aircraft bombed targets in Libya on 15 April, ten days after the bombing of a discotheque in West Berlin on 5 April.

headline: Six million Americans form a human chain
text: On 25 May about 6.5 million people held hands from New York City to Long Beach, California, in Hands Across America, to raise money to fight hunger and homelessness.

headline: Expo 86 opens in Vancouver
text: The world's fair Expo 86 opened in Vancouver, Canada, on 2 May.

headline: NBC unveils its peacock logo
text: On 12 May the NBC network showed its new peacock logo in a special for its 60th anniversary.

headline: Report on the Challenger blames the cold and a faulty seal
text: The Rogers Commission published its report on the Challenger disaster on 6 June. A seal in the right booster rocket failed in record cold, and hot gas burned through. The commission interviewed over 160 people.

headline: Argentina win the World Cup
text: Argentina beat West Germany 3-2 in the World Cup final in Mexico City on 29 June. Diego Maradona scored two goals against England in the quarter-final on 22 June, one of them with his hand.

headline: Waldheim elected president of Austria
text: Kurt Waldheim was elected president of Austria on 8 June, despite the Nazi war crimes allegations raised in March.

headline: Email lists are born
text: Eric Thomas wrote LISTSERV on 23 June. It is software that sends one email to a whole list of people on a network.

headline: The Dow closes above 1,900
text: On 1 July the Dow closed at 1,903.54, its first close above 1,900. It ended 1985 at 1,546.67, so it is up about 23% in six months.

headline: The Statue of Liberty reopens
text: The Statue of Liberty reopened on 4 July after a refurbishment for its centennial.

headline: Disney releases "The Great Mouse Detective"
text: Disney's cartoon The Great Mouse Detective came out on 2 July. Under chief executive Michael Eisner, Disney is also making films for grown-ups under its Touchstone label.

headline: Oil dips below 9 dollars a barrel
text: In July the Brent oil price fell under $9, while OPEC's output rose to 20 million barrels a day. The price was $28 in November 1985.

headline: Prince Andrew marries Sarah Ferguson
text: Prince Andrew married Sarah Ferguson at Westminster Abbey on 23 July.

headline: Lake Nyos gas cloud kills nearly 2,000
text: On 21 August a cloud of gas released by Lake Nyos in Cameroon killed nearly 2,000 people.

headline: Timothy Dalton named as the new James Bond
text: On 6 August Timothy Dalton was announced as the fourth actor to play James Bond.

headline: Nintendo releases Metroid
text: Nintendo released the game Metroid for its Famicom Disk System on 6 August.

headline: The Economist invents the Big Mac Index
text: On 6 September The Economist introduced the Big Mac Index, a joking way to see whether currencies are fairly priced. It compares what a McDonald's Big Mac costs in each country.

headline: Walt Disney Productions becomes The Walt Disney Company
text: On 28 September Walt Disney Productions renamed itself The Walt Disney Company. Under Michael Eisner it has moved from last place to first in box office receipts among the eight major studios, and Captain EO has opened at Disneyland.

headline: Nintendo's console goes on sale across America
text: The Nintendo Entertainment System went on sale throughout North America on 27 September, after test sales in New York and Los Angeles.

headline: Mercedes makes the catalytic converter standard
text: In September Mercedes-Benz made catalytic converters, which clean exhaust gas, standard equipment on its mid-size W124 range. Until now they came only on some versions.

headline: Compaq builds the first PC with Intel's 386 chip
text: In September Compaq introduced the Deskpro 386, the first personal computer with Intel's 80386 processor. It is the first time a company other than IBM brings a major step forward in PC hardware.

headline: Hijackers seize a Pan Am jet in Karachi
text: Pan Am flight 73 was hijacked in Karachi, Pakistan, on 5 September.

headline: London's Big Bang changes the stock exchange
text: On 27 October the London Stock Exchange scrapped fixed commissions, replaced shouting on the floor with computer screens, and let foreign firms in. Swiss banks have bought British brokers to take part: UBS took 29.9% of Phillips & Drew in 1984 and announced a full takeover this year.

headline: Reagan signs a big tax reform
text: President Reagan signed the Tax Reform Act on 22 October. It cuts the top income tax rate from 50% to 28%, reduces the number of tax brackets from 15 to 4, and removes many deductions.

headline: Reagan and Gorbachev fail to agree at Reykjavik
text: At their meeting in Reykjavik on 11 and 12 October Gorbachev proposed to abolish all nuclear weapons within ten years. The talks ended without agreement over Reagan's Strategic Defense Initiative, a missile defence research plan.

headline: Saudi Arabia fires its oil minister
text: On 29 October King Fahd dismissed the oil minister Ahmed Zaki Yamani, who had refused to accept a higher Saudi quota and an oil price of $18.

headline: The Mets win the World Series
text: The New York Mets won the World Series against the Boston Red Sox on 27 October, after a ground ball slipped through Bill Buckner's legs in game six.

headline: Fox Broadcasting launches
text: The Fox Broadcasting Company started on 9 October, after Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation completed its purchase of Metromedia.

headline: Fire at a Sandoz warehouse turns the Rhine red
text: A fire at a Sandoz storehouse for farm chemicals in Schweizerhalle near Basel on 1 November sent poisonous chemicals into the Rhine with the firefighting water. A great many fish and eels died downstream. The cause of the fire is not known.

headline: Reagan's secret arms sales to Iran come out
text: On 3 November a Lebanese magazine reported that the US had sold weapons to Iran in exchange for the release of hostages. On 25 November the Attorney General said that part of the money had gone to the Contra rebels in Nicaragua, and Oliver North was fired.

headline: Mike Tyson becomes heavyweight champion at 20
text: On 22 November Mike Tyson became the youngest heavyweight boxing champion ever, at age 20.

headline: OPEC agrees to cut output and aim for 18 dollars
text: On 19 December OPEC agreed to cut output by 7% for the first half of 1987 and to raise prices toward $18 a barrel. In November 1985 the price was about $30 before it fell below $10.

headline: The Dow ends 1986 at 1,895.95, up 23%
text: The Dow Jones index closed the year at 1,895.95, up 22.58%, on top of last year's 27.66%.

headline: Tokyo stocks end 1986 at 18,821
text: The Nikkei index of Japanese shares ended 1986 at 18,821, from above 13,000 a year ago, and the yen is much stronger than before the Plaza agreement. A rising market is good news for IBJ, which lends to big industry and holds shares in its clients.

headline: Schlumberger cuts jobs as oilfield work dries up
text: Schlumberger, which measures and drills oil wells for the oil companies, cut jobs in 1986 because of the oil price crash. In the US, the number of drilling rigs fell from nearly 2,300 in late 1985 to barely 1,000.

headline: Berkshire buys Scott Fetzer for around 320 million dollars
text: During 1986 Berkshire Hathaway bought the Scott Fetzer Company for about $320 million, though sources give figures from $315 million. Scott Fetzer is a group of 32 brands that makes products for homes, industry and institutions.

headline: The Rutan Voyager sets off around the world
text: The Rutan Voyager aircraft began its flight around the world on 14 December.
